To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BgEcRA is required for normal development during the last nymphhal instar and the adult stage, that BgEcRa is required for normal ecdysteroid titer, and that BgEcra is required for normal cell proliferation in the ovarian follicular epithelum.

BgEcR is expressed in all tissues analyzed during the penultimate and final nymphal instars, and is required for nymph survival, and that knockdown specimens exhibit molting defects, reduced cell proliferation in the epithelium and defects in adult-specific developmental processes.

the ecdysteroid receptor isoform-A is required for normal development of the German cockroach during the last nymphhal instar and for some processes during the transition to the adult stage, such as molting, cell proliferation, ecdysteroid production, and adult-specific processes, such as choriogenesis and prothoracic degeneration.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in hemimetabolus insects, the ecdysoid receptor-A plays an important role during the last nymph stage, but it is not required for adult development.
BgEcRE-A during the last larval instar is involved in the regulation of molting and metamorphosis, whereas in adults it is involved in the control of adult-specific developmental events.
BgEcRs-A is required during the last nymph instar for nymphal survival and for the development of the adult.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BgEcRs are required for normal development in the German cockroach, and the functions of BgsEcRs are similar to those of their orthologs in D. melanogaster.
BgEcRs are required during the last nymph instar for molting, survival and normal cell proliferation in the fat body and follicular epitheliam.

The main takeaway from our work is that

BgEcREcR-A has functions during the nymphal and adult stages that are similar to those described for Drosophila, but also functions during nymphal development that are not described for holometabolous species.

the functions of B. germanica ecdysone signaling are similar to those of the ecdysteroid signaling system in D. melanogaster, and that the B. germanica EcR isoform-A plays a role in the control of cell proliferation and molting, and is required for the proper development of the adult stage.
BgEcrA is a pleiotropic gene with a broad role in the development of the last nymphal and adult stages of B. germanica.
